title: Member Self-Service — RideLink Alternative-Ride Claims after a Late Pickup
content:
When a Non-Emergency Medical Transportation pickup runs late, the member may take an alternative ride and claim an alternative-ride reimbursement, which the member files themselves from their RideLink account.

## Rule

An alternative-ride claim is worked out for the member's latest recorded late pickup, from that late leg and the registered legs of the same trip, and it records the trip's reservation number, the late leg, the late leg's date as its trip date and the amount. After a late pickup the member may take an alternative ride and be reimbursed the alternative-ride allowance as an alternative-ride reimbursement, whatever the receipt shows. An alternative-ride claim rests on the late pickup record of its leg and needs no paid claim to prove attendance.

For a late value-added leg in the current benefit year, the alternative-ride allowance is fixed only after the ledger carries the allotment load for the benefit year of that leg's trip date. Put the other way round: while the ledger carries no allotment load for that benefit year, the allowance for such a leg is not yet fixed.

**Effect.** The claim stands on the reimbursement ledger as an approved claim with a new member reimbursement claim number and is owed to the member until it is paid. The member sees the claim, its number and amount in their reimbursement history.

## The member's tool

The claim is filed with `file_alternative_ride_claim_fa98ae6a`, a tool the member runs from their own RideLink account. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves — the member — then runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`, entering the amount. One call files one claim, dated today; nothing else on the benefit changes.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `ride_benefit_id` | Reference number of the member's transportation benefit, as the transportation benefit lookup returns it and the agent reads it to the member | Identifier |
| `trip_number` | The reservation number of the trip whose pickup was late, as on the member's ride confirmation or the ride history | Verbatim, character for character (for example RL-5580213) |
| `leg` | The leg whose pickup was late | One of `outbound` (on the way to the destination), `return` (on the way back home), `round_trip` (the claim covers both legs), `not_applicable` (no leg) |
| `reimbursement_type` | The kind of reimbursement claimed | One of `late_pickup_alternative` (the kind this filing records), `mileage`, `lodging_meals`, `not_applicable` (kinds this filing never records) |
| `claim_trip_date` | The date of the late leg | YYYY-MM-DD, a calendar date with no time or time zone |
| `amount` | The amount claimed | USD, 2 decimal places, positive; stored rounded to 2 decimals exactly as entered |

**Return.** A text dictionary: `status` is the literal "filed" when the claim was recorded, which is the success receipt; `reimbursement_claim_number` is the new claim number in the form MR-YYMMDD-NNNN; `ledger_entry` is the reference of the new claim entry; `trip_number`, `leg`, `reimbursement_type` and `claim_trip_date` echo what was filed; `amount` is the USD amount with 2 decimals; `posted_date` is today's date as YYYY-MM-DD.
